promise: each graphic object is recognisable as what it is (owner rule)
brief: design/RimMandrake/art_judge_brief.md (B1a no outlines, B2 legibility advisory, C2, D1)

measurements.method: PIL alpha>128 bbox and Rec.601 luminance on the raw 256 px textures; ground = walk capture rows 520-700

per_pose.reason: a ~7 px wide pale vertical stalk; the black lower legs (43% of the figure) sink into the black ash, so no legs, body or head register. The in-game capture confirms it: six grey stakes.
the profile keeps the neck-back-rump line and a leg pair, so it reads as a small gazelle or giraffe glyph. It is faint but has an animal shape.
the same stalk as the south facing (about 6 px wide), with no rump mass or legs that separate from the ground.
the turned east profile is a thin grey scribble (neck and stick legs, little barrel) and reads as a twig or bone on the ground. Each vanilla neighbour lying still shows a body mass.
the head and crest, the neck, the pale chest and four dark legs are separable: a thin long-necked grazer facing the viewer. It is weak beside the vanilla animals.
the rump, the legs and the neck rising to the head read as a long-necked animal from behind. It is thin but legible.
it reads as a long-necked animal on its side (head, neck and legs visible). The turn is the engine's rule and applies to vanilla too.

flaws.promise: each graphic object is recognisable as what it is
flaws.seen: At the default map zoom of these captures (20 px/cell), 3 of 4 poses do not read as an animal. In the real capture (walk_station_creatures.jpg, ~22 px/cell) the herd of six south-facing ullai reads as thin grey posts, not animals.
causes: Silhouette width: the south and north facings use 15-17% of the canvas width, against 27-37% for the narrowest vanilla grazers (female elk and deer, dromedary, gazelle). At drawSize 2.0 that is about 7 px at 20 ppc, so the legs are sub-pixel.

Contrast against the ground: the black lower legs are 34-43% of the opaque pixels, at the value of the Pyrelands ash (ground p10 L=37, median 77). The legs vanish and leave a floating pale stalk with no quadruped cue.

Little body mass: the light-boned design puts most of the 2-cell height into neck and legs. The barrel and haunch are too small to make a 'body' shape at 20 ppc, and this also makes the lying (turned east) pose a scribble.
flaws.not_a_cause: Missing keyline. Vanilla animals carry one, but owner card 2026-10-04 (brief B1a) rules out drawn outlines, so a keyline is not a valid fix.

polish: polish: at 48 ppc the south and north facings read, but stick-thin beside the vanilla animals. The broader S/N redraw below would also fix this.
polish: the crest and head are very small at both zooms. A slightly larger head mass would help the face read on the south facing.
polish: the composites have no shadow or lighting. A live shadow may help a little at 20 ppc, but the walk capture (which has both) still shows posts, so this does not change the verdict.
smallest_fix: Redraw only the south and north facings with more body width: a wider stance (legs splayed under a visible barrel and haunch, chest and rump shown with volume, the neck slightly foreshortened), so the front and rear views carry a body mass like vanilla deer and elk. Then restrict the black to the hooves and pasterns (pale or ash-grey cannons above), so the legs separate from the black ash; this needs an owner-acceptable reading of 'black lower legs'. Deepen the barrel a little in the east facing, which also fixes the lying pose. No outline (B1a). A larger drawSize is only a suggestion and would not alone fix the colour-on-ash loss.
